title: Nottingham lettings agents handle twice national average
summary:
Nottingham lettings agents are managing an average of 31.4 available rental properties each, more than double the national average across major British cities. Analysis of 21 major cities found significant regional disparities in agent workloads.

The post Nottingham lettings agents handle twice national average appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Over a third of agents miss six-hour proposal window
summary:
More than one in three estate agency proposals are sent after the six-hour window associated with higher instruction conversion rates, according to research analysing over 123,000 proposals. The study found regional variations, with the North West achieving the fastest turnaround at 2 hours 41 minutes, while Scotland took 5 hours 21 minutes.

The post Over a third of agents miss six-hour proposal window appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Burnham rules out Stamp Duty changes in next Budget
summary:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has confirmed that Stamp Duty will not be reformed in the upcoming Budget, dismissing weekend reports suggesting the tax was under review. The decision follows concerns that speculation about potential changes could freeze the housing market.

The post Burnham rules out Stamp Duty changes in next Budget appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Lancashire landlord fined £5,600 for repair failures
summary:
A private landlord has been fined £5,600 by Blackburn magistrates after failing to comply with an improvement notice for a Clitheroe property. Wajid Mahmood pleaded guilty to the offence after council inspections found multiple hazards including no hot water, damp, mould and faulty electrics.

The post Lancashire landlord fined £5,600 for repair failures appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Landmark launches search bundle for property reforms
summary:
Landmark Information Group has introduced a search bundle designed to assist estate agents and property professionals in preparing for the Government's proposed home buying and selling reforms. The Sales Pack Ready kit combines searches and property information as transaction times reach 123 days on average.

The post Landmark launches search bundle for property reforms appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: London renters face extended tenancy periods, says agent
summary:
A significant proportion of London tenants may never transition to homeownership, according to a director at estate agency Winkworth. Rupal Patel said renters are now forced to remain in the rental sector for substantially longer periods than in previous decades.

The post London renters face extended tenancy periods, says agent appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Student lettings platform UniHomes achieves +61 NPS rating
summary:
Student accommodation platform UniHomes has recorded a Net Promoter Score of +61 in its 2026 annual survey of more than 100 letting agents across the UK. The score saw 70% of surveyed agents rate the platform 9 or 10 out of 10, with enquiry generation identified as the most important benefit by 71% of respondents.

title: Close Brothers provides £20m for Radlett housing scheme
summary:
Close Brothers Property Finance has provided a £20 million revolving credit facility to housebuilder gs8 for the development of 52 homes in Radlett, Hertfordshire. The scheme carries a gross development value of £47 million and includes a zero energy bills guarantee.

The post Close Brothers provides £20m for Radlett housing scheme appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Cheshire pub conversion secures £2m bridging finance
summary:
Black & White Bridging has provided a £2 million bridging finance facility for the conversion of a former Cheshire public house into a holiday let property. The transaction involved refinancing existing debt and releasing additional capital to complete the development.

The post Cheshire pub conversion secures £2m bridging finance appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Bank of England expected to hold rates at 3.75% Thursday
summary:
The Bank of England is anticipated to maintain interest rates at 3.75% when the Monetary Policy Committee announces its decision on Thursday, though geopolitical tensions are introducing fresh uncertainty. Most economists predict a 7-2 vote split in favour of holding rates, following June inflation data showing CPI at 2.6%, its lowest level for 15 months.
